answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away because it is exactly the phrase you wait years to see on your appointment letter, so it signals the makers actually know the service. 'Minister Salary' is the more obvious hook and would get more taps from the general public, but it sounds like a meme about the pay debate and I have heard that joke at every kopitiam since 2012.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A cheeky satire built around the ministerial pay controversy, probably a clicker or a political-sim where you chase the million-dollar benchmark. I'd expect it to be shallow and a bit jeering at the service, and I'd wince if it got the benchmark formula wrong.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A drier, insider-flavoured career sim about the slow grind through the ranks: probation, confirmation, acting appointments versus substantive ones, appraisal wording. I'd expect it to be a niche game with in-jokes that only civil servants get, and I'd be curious whether it handles the details correctly. Outsiders might find the name baffling, though.

tone_breaks.line: At 38, in The Officer You Nominated
tone_breaks.note: The ending card says age 38 for this event, but the notes show it as a later year in a career that ended at 59, and the age timeline did not match the years. Also the title Prime Minister as a ceiling the file sets sits oddly with how real selection works, though it is a game.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary
tone_breaks.note: The benchmark is tied to median incomes of top earners, not a multiple of the entry-grade minister's pay, so this reads slightly off to an insider.
